questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The climate of the Kashmir Valley is best described as:
options: Temperate with cold winters and mild summers
Tropical hot and humid throughout the year
Arid desert climate with extreme heat
questions.correctAnswer: Temperate with cold winters and mild summers
questions.explanation: The Kashmir Valley has a temperate climate with cold, snowy winters and pleasantly mild summers. 'Tropical hot and humid' is wrong — Kashmir is at high altitude (1,500–2,000m) and experiences cold winters, unlike tropical zones. 'Arid desert' is wrong — Kashmir receives good rainfall and snowfall. 'Equatorial' is wrong — Kashmir is at 34°N latitude, far from the equator.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the climate of Jammu region:

(i) The Jammu plains experience sub-tropical climate.
(ii) Summers in Jammu are hot with temperatures often exceeding 40°C.
(iii) The Jammu region receives most of its rainfall during the monsoon season.
(iv) Jammu region experiences heavy snowfall every winter.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Jammu's plains (Jammu, Kathua, Samba) have a sub-tropical climate. (ii) is correct — summer temperatures in Jammu city frequently exceed 40°C. (iii) is correct — the monsoon (July–September) brings most of Jammu's annual rainfall. (iv) is wrong — the Jammu plains do NOT receive heavy snowfall; snowfall occurs in the higher hill areas (Patnitop, Bhaderwah), not in the plains of Jammu city.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which of the following is the most famous cash crop of the Kashmir Valley?
questions.explanation: Saffron (Kesar) is Kashmir's most famous and valuable cash crop, primarily grown in the Pampore region. It is the most expensive spice in the world. 'Sugarcane' is wrong — it is a tropical/subtropical crop grown in UP, Maharashtra, not Kashmir. 'Cotton' is wrong — cotton requires hot, dry climate (Gujarat, Maharashtra), not Kashmir's temperate climate. 'Jute' is wrong — jute grows in hot, humid tropical conditions (West Bengal, Bihar).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Apple is the most important fruit crop of Jammu & Kashmir.
Reason (R): The temperate climate of Kashmir with cold winters and mild summers provides ideal conditions for apple cultivation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — apples are J&K's most important fruit crop, accounting for a large share of India's apple production. Reason (R) is also correct — apples require chilling hours in winter and moderate summers, which Kashmir's temperate climate provides. (R) explains (A) because the suitable climate is the direct reason for successful apple cultivation. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is correct. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following regions of J&K with their predominant climate type:

Column I:
(a) Jammu plains
(b) Kashmir Valley
(c) Ladakh
(d) Pir Panjal range

Column II:
(i) Cold desert / arid
(ii) Sub-tropical
(iii) Alpine with heavy snowfall
(iv) Temperate

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Jammu plains have sub-tropical climate (hot summers, moderate winters) — matches (ii). (b) Kashmir Valley has temperate climate (cold winters, mild summers) — matches (iv). (c) Ladakh has cold desert/arid climate (extreme cold, very low rainfall) — matches (i). (d) Pir Panjal range has alpine climate with heavy snowfall — matches (iii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following crops are primarily grown in the Kashmir Valley?

(i) Rice (paddy)
(ii) Saffron
(iii) Walnuts
(iv) Rubber

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — rice is the staple food crop of Kashmir, grown extensively in the valley's flat wetlands. (ii) is correct — saffron is grown in Pampore and surrounding areas of Kashmir. (iii) is correct — walnuts are a major dry fruit crop of Kashmir (India's leading producer). (iv) is wrong — rubber is a tropical plantation crop grown in Kerala and Northeast India, not in Kashmir's cold climate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Western Disturbances that bring winter rainfall to J&K originate from:
options: The Mediterranean Sea and the Caspian Sea region
questions.correctAnswer: The Mediterranean Sea and the Caspian Sea region
questions.explanation: Western Disturbances are extratropical storms originating over the Mediterranean/Caspian region that travel eastward and bring winter precipitation (rain and snow) to northern India, including J&K. 'Bay of Bengal' is wrong — it feeds the summer monsoon in eastern/northeastern India. 'Arabian Sea' is wrong — it primarily feeds the southwest monsoon. 'Pacific Ocean' is wrong — it influences East Asian weather, not Indian subcontinent.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about saffron cultivation in J&K:

(i) Saffron is primarily grown in the Pampore-Pulwama belt of Kashmir.
(ii) Saffron requires well-drained karewa soil.
(iii) Saffron is harvested in the spring season (March–April).
(iv) The dried stigmas of the saffron crocus flower are used as a spice.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Pampore (in Pulwama district) is the main saffron-growing area of India. (ii) is correct — saffron thrives in the well-drained karewa (elevated plateau) soils of Kashmir. (iv) is correct — the three red stigmas from each crocus flower are dried to produce saffron spice. (iii) is wrong — saffron is harvested in AUTUMN (October–November), not spring. The crocus flowers bloom in October.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The average annual rainfall in the Kashmir Valley is approximately __________.
questions.explanation: The Kashmir Valley receives moderate rainfall of approximately 600–700 mm annually, with precipitation spread across winter (snow), spring, and some monsoon influence. '200–300 mm' is wrong — that describes arid regions like Ladakh. '1500–2000 mm' is wrong — that describes high-rainfall areas like Meghalaya or the Western Ghats. '50–100 mm' is wrong — that's extreme desert-level precipitation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ladakh receives very little rainfall despite being surrounded by high mountains.
Reason (R): Ladakh lies in the rain shadow of the Greater Himalayas, which block moisture-laden winds from reaching it.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Ladakh is a cold desert receiving only about 100 mm annual precipitation. Reason (R) is also correct — the Greater Himalayas block both the southwest monsoon and most western disturbances. (R) explains (A) because the rain-shadow effect is the direct cause of Ladakh's aridity. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is geographically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which fruit is J&K the largest producer of in India?
questions.explanation: J&K produces approximately 75% of India's total apple output, making it the largest apple-producing state/UT in the country. 'Mango' is wrong — UP, AP, and Karnataka are the top mango producers. 'Banana' is wrong — Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, and Maharashtra lead in banana production. 'Grapes' is wrong — Maharashtra (Nashik) dominates grape production.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following crops with the regions where they are primarily grown in J&K:

Column I:
(a) Saffron
(b) Basmati rice
(c) Maize
(d) Apple

Column II:
(i) Hilly areas of Kashmir (Sopore, Shopian, Kupwara)
(ii) Pampore-Pulwama belt
(iii) R.S. Pura belt of Jammu
(iv) Jammu hills and lower areas

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Saffron is grown in the Pampore-Pulwama karewa belt — matches (ii). (b) Basmati rice is cultivated in the R.S. Pura belt of Jammu — matches (iii). (c) Maize is grown in Jammu hills and lower areas — matches (iv). (d) Apple orchards are in Sopore, Shopian, Kupwara, and other hilly areas of Kashmir — matches (i). Option 2 swaps saffron and basmati. Option 3 swaps basmati and maize. Option 4 swaps maize and apple.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Chillai Kalan' in Kashmir refers to:
options: The 40-day period of harshest winter cold (December 21 to January 31)
The monsoon season in the valley
questions.correctAnswer: The 40-day period of harshest winter cold (December 21 to January 31)
questions.explanation: 'Chillai Kalan' is the 40-day period of intense winter cold in Kashmir, traditionally from December 21 to January 31, when temperatures frequently drop below −10°C and the Dal Lake may freeze. 'Monsoon season' is wrong — that's a summer phenomenon. 'Rice harvest festival' is wrong — that's not what Chillai Kalan means. 'Tulip blooming' is wrong — tulips bloom in spring (March–April).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about walnut production in J&K:

(i) J&K is the leading walnut-producing region of India.
(ii) Walnuts are a temperate nut crop suited to Kashmir's climate.
(iii) Kashmir's walnuts are famous for their thin shell and rich flavour.
(iv) Walnuts require a tropical climate to grow.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — J&K produces over 90% of India's walnuts. (ii) is correct — walnuts are a temperate crop requiring cold winters for dormancy. (iii) is correct — Kashmiri walnuts are prized worldwide for their quality. (iv) is wrong — walnuts require TEMPERATE climate (cold winters), not tropical. Tropical climates are too warm for walnut trees.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'karewa' soils of Kashmir are significant for agriculture because:
options: They are well-drained elevated plateaus ideal for saffron and dry fruit cultivation
They are flooded plains ideal for rice paddy
They contain volcanic ash good for tea plantations
They are sandy soils suited for desert crops
questions.correctAnswer: They are well-drained elevated plateaus ideal for saffron and dry fruit cultivation
questions.explanation: Karewas are lacustrine (ancient lake-bed) deposits forming elevated flat-topped mounds in Kashmir, with well-drained soil perfect for saffron, almonds, and orchards. 'Flooded plains for rice' is wrong — rice is grown in flat valley floors, not on karewas. 'Volcanic ash for tea' is wrong — karewas are sedimentary, not volcanic; tea needs acidic soil in humid conditions. 'Sandy desert soils' is wrong — karewas are clay-silt deposits, not sandy.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Rice (paddy) is the staple food crop of the Kashmir Valley.
Reason (R): The flat valley floor with abundant water supply from rivers and springs provides ideal conditions for paddy cultivation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — rice is the primary food grain of Kashmiris, with the valley producing significant quantities. Reason (R) is also correct — rice requires standing water, and the flat terrain with rivers (Jhelum) and springs provides natural irrigation. (R) explains (A) because the water availability and flat terrain make rice cultivation feasible and dominant. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option 3 is wrong because (R) is geographically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are dry fruits/nuts commercially produced in J&K?

(i) Walnut
(ii) Almond
(iii) Cashew
(iv) Apricot

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — walnuts are a major dry fruit crop of Kashmir. (ii) is correct — almonds are grown in Kashmir's temperate conditions (especially Budgam, Srinagar). (iv) is correct — apricots are extensively grown in Ladakh and some parts of Kashmir. (iii) is wrong — cashew nuts require tropical coastal climate (Goa, Kerala, Maharashtra) and are NOT grown in J&K's cold climate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The summer temperature in Srinagar typically ranges between:
questions.explanation: Srinagar has pleasant summers with temperatures typically between 20°C and 35°C (occasionally reaching 37°C in June–July). '35°C to 45°C' is wrong — that describes plains like Jammu or Delhi. '10°C to 15°C' is wrong — that's more typical of autumn/spring, not summer. '40°C to 50°C' is wrong — such extreme heat doesn't occur in Kashmir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the monsoon in J&K:

(i) The Jammu region receives substantial monsoon rainfall from the Southwest Monsoon.
(ii) The Kashmir Valley receives very little direct monsoon rainfall.
(iii) The Pir Panjal range acts as a barrier limiting monsoon penetration into Kashmir.
(iv) The entire J&K region receives uniform heavy monsoon rainfall.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Jammu region, being on the windward side, receives good monsoon rain (July–September). (ii) is correct — the Kashmir Valley gets limited monsoon rainfall as it lies beyond the Pir Panjal barrier. (iii) is correct — the Pir Panjal range blocks much of the moisture-laden monsoon winds from reaching the valley. (iv) is wrong — rainfall distribution is highly uneven; Jammu gets monsoon rain while Kashmir and Ladakh get very little.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The famous 'Basmati' rice variety is primarily cultivated in the __________ region of J&K.
questions.explanation: The R.S. Pura belt in Jammu district is famous for cultivating high-quality Basmati rice. 'Kashmir Valley' is wrong — Kashmir grows non-Basmati varieties suited to its cooler conditions. 'Ladakh' is wrong — Ladakh's extreme cold and arid climate is unsuitable for rice. 'Kargil' is wrong — Kargil's climate doesn't support paddy cultivation at all.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Snowfall is crucial for Kashmir's agriculture and water supply.
Reason (R): Snowmelt in spring and summer feeds rivers and streams that irrigate the valley's crops and orchards.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — winter snow is vital for Kashmir's water reserves and agriculture. Reason (R) is also correct — snow stored in mountains melts gradually, providing water through spring/summer when crops need it. (R) explains (A) because the snowmelt mechanism is the specific way snow supports agriculture. Option 2 is wrong because (R) gives the direct mechanism. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following seasons in Kashmir with their local names:

Column I:
(a) Spring
(b) Summer
(c) Autumn
(d) Winter

Column II:
(i) Wandh
(ii) Sonth
(iii) Grishm/Rathwol
(iv) Harud

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Spring in Kashmiri is 'Sonth' — matches (ii). (b) Summer is 'Grishm' or 'Rathwol' — matches (iii). (c) Autumn is 'Harud' (famous for chinar leaves turning golden) — matches (iv). (d) Winter is 'Wandh' — matches (i). Option 2 swaps spring and summer. Option 3 swaps summer and autumn. Option 4 swaps autumn and winter.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are major horticultural crops of J&K?

(i) Apple
(ii) Cherry
(iii) Pear
(iv) Coconut

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — apple is J&K's primary horticultural crop. (ii) is correct — cherries are grown commercially in Kashmir (Srinagar, Ganderbal). (iii) is correct — pears (Nashpati) are widely cultivated in Kashmir. (iv) is wrong — coconut is a tropical palm grown in Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu. It cannot survive Kashmir's freezing winters.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Chillai Khurd' and 'Chillai Bachha' in Kashmir refer to:
options: Periods of cold following Chillai Kalan — 20 days and 10 days respectively
questions.correctAnswer: Periods of cold following Chillai Kalan — 20 days and 10 days respectively
questions.explanation: After Chillai Kalan (40 days, Dec 21–Jan 31), Chillai Khurd (20 days, Feb 1–19) and Chillai Bachha (10 days, Feb 20–Mar 1) follow as progressively milder cold periods. 'Summer harvest' is wrong — these are winter cold periods. 'Spring festivals' is wrong — they mark winter severity, not celebrations. 'Monsoon onset' is wrong — monsoon comes in July, months later.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about maize cultivation in J&K:

(i) Maize is the main kharif (summer) food crop of the Jammu region.
(ii) Maize is grown in the hilly and sub-mountainous areas.
(iii) It requires heavy irrigation and cannot grow on rain-fed land.
(iv) Maize is used both as food for humans and fodder for animals.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — maize is the primary kharif food crop in Jammu's hilly tracts. (ii) is correct — maize thrives in the undulating, hilly terrain of the Jammu region. (iv) is correct — maize grains are used for food (makki ki roti) and the plant is used as cattle fodder. (iii) is wrong — maize is largely a RAIN-FED crop in J&K; it does NOT require heavy irrigation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Tulip Garden (Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden) in Srinagar is significant because:
options: It is Asia's largest tulip garden, blooming in spring (March–April)
It is India's oldest botanical garden from the Mughal era
It grows tulips throughout the year due to Kashmir's unique climate
It is primarily a rose garden renamed after tulips were planted
questions.correctAnswer: It is Asia's largest tulip garden, blooming in spring (March–April)
questions.explanation: The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden at the foothills of Zabarwan range in Srinagar is Asia's largest tulip garden, with millions of tulips blooming in spring. 'Oldest Mughal garden' is wrong — Mughal gardens (Shalimar, Nishat) are separate; the Tulip Garden was opened in 2007. 'Year-round tulips' is wrong — tulips bloom only during spring for 2–3 weeks. 'Renamed rose garden' is wrong — it was specifically developed as a tulip garden.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about wheat cultivation in J&K:

(i) Wheat is a rabi (winter) crop in J&K.
(ii) Wheat is grown primarily in the Jammu region.
(iii) The Kashmir Valley is the leading wheat-producing area.
(iv) Wheat is sown in October–November and harvested in April–May.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — wheat is a rabi (winter) crop sown after monsoon and harvested before summer. (ii) is correct — the Jammu plains (R.S. Pura, Kathua, Samba) are the main wheat-producing areas. (iv) is correct — wheat is typically sown in October–November and harvested in April–May in J&K. (iii) is wrong — the Kashmir Valley primarily grows rice, not wheat; Jammu is the leading wheat area.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following spices, apart from saffron, are grown in J&K?

(i) Zeera (cumin)
(ii) Kalazeera (black cumin/caraway)
(iii) Cardamom
(iv) Fennel

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — cumin (zeera) is cultivated in parts of J&K. (ii) is correct — kalazeera (black cumin/Bunium persicum) is a valuable spice grown in the higher altitudes of Kashmir and Ladakh. (iv) is correct — fennel (saunf) is grown in Jammu region. (iii) is wrong — cardamom is a tropical spice grown in Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu; it cannot grow in J&K's climate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Kashmir Valley is sometimes called 'Paradise on Earth'.
Reason (R): Its temperate climate, scenic beauty with snow-capped mountains, lush green meadows, sparkling rivers, and pleasant summers make it exceptionally beautiful.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Kashmir has been called 'Paradise on Earth' (attributed to Mughal Emperor Jahangir). Reason (R) is also correct — the combination of temperate climate, natural beauty, and scenic landscapes justifies the title. (R) explains (A) because these natural features are what led to this description. Option 2 is wrong because (R) gives the specific reasons. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The average winter temperature in Srinagar during January is approximately:
questions.explanation: Srinagar's January temperatures typically range from −2°C (minimum, often below freezing) to about 4°C (maximum). '10°C to 15°C' is wrong — that's more typical of autumn. '−20°C to −15°C' is wrong — such extreme cold is more typical of Ladakh (Dras/Leh), not Srinagar city. '15°C to 20°C' is wrong — that's spring/early summer temperature.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which mountain pass connects the Jammu region to the Kashmir Valley?
questions.explanation: The Banihal Pass (with the Jawahar Tunnel at 2,194m) on the Pir Panjal range connects Jammu to the Kashmir Valley via NH44. 'Zoji La Pass' is wrong — it connects Kashmir Valley to Ladakh. 'Khardung La' is wrong — it's in Ladakh connecting Leh to the Nubra Valley. 'Rohtang Pass' is wrong — it connects Manali (Himachal Pradesh) to Lahaul-Spiti.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following fruits with their peak harvesting season in J&K:

Column I:
(a) Apple
(b) Cherry
(c) Apricot
(d) Strawberry

Column II:
(i) May–June
(ii) June–July
(iii) August–October
(iv) April–May

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Apple harvest peaks August–October — matches (iii). (b) Cherry season is May–June in Kashmir — matches (i). (c) Apricot ripens in June–July — matches (ii). (d) Strawberry season is April–May in Kashmir — matches (iv). Option 2 swaps apple and cherry. Option 3 swaps cherry and apricot. Option 4 swaps apricot and strawberry.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the impact of climate on transport in J&K:

(i) The Srinagar–Jammu highway (NH44) is frequently closed during winter due to snowfall and landslides.
(ii) The Srinagar–Leh highway closes from November to May due to snow at Zoji La.
(iii) Jammu airport never faces disruptions due to fog.
(iv) Rail connectivity to Kashmir through the Banihal–Qazigund tunnel helps reduce weather-related disruptions.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — NH44 through Banihal is often blocked by snow/landslides in winter. (ii) is correct — the Srinagar–Leh highway via Zoji La (3,528m) closes for about 6 months in winter. (iv) is correct — the Banihal railway tunnel provides all-weather rail connectivity that is less affected by surface weather. (iii) is wrong — Jammu airport DOES face disruptions from fog, especially in December–January.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a major crop of the Ladakh region?
questions.explanation: Rice (paddy) requires warm temperatures and standing water, which Ladakh's cold, arid climate cannot provide. 'Barley' is wrong — barley IS grown in Ladakh as it tolerates cold and dry conditions. 'Buckwheat' is wrong — it IS grown in Ladakh's harsh climate. 'Apricot' is wrong — Ladakh IS famous for its apricots.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the 'Mughal Gardens' of Kashmir:

(i) They were built during the Mughal era by emperors who loved Kashmir's climate.
(ii) Shalimar Bagh and Nishat Bagh are famous Mughal gardens in Srinagar.
(iii) These gardens feature terraced layouts with water channels.
(iv) They were originally designed as military forts.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Mughal emperors (Jahangir, Shah Jahan) built gardens in Kashmir attracted by its pleasant climate. (ii) is correct — Shalimar Bagh (garden of love) and Nishat Bagh (garden of bliss) are iconic Mughal gardens on Dal Lake's shores. (iii) is correct — they feature the classic Mughal style: terraced levels with fountains, water channels (charbagh layout). (iv) is wrong — they were pleasure gardens for royalty, NOT military forts.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The major river that flows through the Kashmir Valley and supports its agriculture is:
questions.explanation: The Jhelum (Vitasta in Sanskrit) is the principal river of the Kashmir Valley, flowing through Srinagar and providing water for agriculture. 'Chenab' is wrong — it flows through the Jammu region (Doda, Kishtwar, Ramban). 'Tawi' is wrong — it is a smaller river flowing through Jammu city. 'Indus' is wrong — it flows through Ladakh, not the Kashmir Valley.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following flowers are commercially grown in J&K?

(i) Tulip
(ii) Lavender
(iii) Rose
(iv) Lotus (in Dal Lake)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — tulips are commercially grown in the Tulip Garden and exported. (ii) is correct — lavender cultivation has been introduced in J&K (Bhaderwah, Doda). (iii) is correct — roses are grown commercially in Kashmir. (iv) is correct — lotus grows naturally and is harvested from Dal Lake (lotus stems/nadru are a local delicacy). All four are correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The term 'Sonmarg' literally means 'Meadow of Gold'. Why is it named so?
options: Its meadows appear golden with wildflowers in spring/summer
It was a historical gold trading centre
questions.correctAnswer: Its meadows appear golden with wildflowers in spring/summer
questions.explanation: Sonamarg (Sonmarg) means 'Meadow of Gold' because its vast alpine meadows turn golden with blooming wildflowers (crocuses, daisies) in spring and summer. 'Gold mining' is wrong — there are no gold mines there. 'Gold dust in soil' is wrong — the name refers to the floral appearance. 'Gold trading centre' is wrong — it was a waypoint on the ancient Silk Route, but named for its floral beauty.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about livestock and animal husbandry in J&K:

(i) The Bakerwal and Gujjar communities are traditional pastoralists of J&K.
(ii) Sheep rearing is important for Kashmir's wool and pashmina industry.
(iii) Pashmina wool comes from the Changthangi goats of Ladakh.
(iv) J&K has no dairy farming activity.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Bakerwals and Gujjars are nomadic pastoral tribes who rear sheep and goats in J&K's mountainous regions. (ii) is correct — sheep provide wool for Kashmir's famous shawl industry. (iii) is correct — the finest pashmina comes from Changthangi goats (Changra) reared by Changpa nomads in Ladakh's Changthang plateau. (iv) is wrong — J&K DOES have dairy farming; milk production is significant.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Harvesting Season' (Harud) in Kashmir is associated with which months?
questions.explanation: Harud (autumn) in Kashmir spans approximately September to November, coinciding with the apple and rice harvest. It is famous for golden chinar leaves. 'March–May' is wrong — that's spring (Sonth). 'June–August' is wrong — that's summer (Grishm). 'December–February' is wrong — that's the peak of winter (Wandh/Chillai Kalan).
